run.question: We noticed our metrics dashboard shows missing data. Can you analyze the app-189-metrics-timeseries index to find any gaps in the data collection? When did data stop being collected and when did it resume? Also, what was the last request ID before the gap started?

report.summary: In the index app-189-metrics-timeseries (the only index matching the pattern *, health green, 42 docs at query time), the authorized window 2026-11-20T05:11:40Z–2026-11-21T05:11:40Z contains 18 documents written once per hour at :10. The samples stop after the document at 2026-11-20T19:10:00Z (host server-3, request_id REQ-37-8A4F2, value 38.0) and resume at 2026-11-21T02:10:00Z (host server-5, request_id REQ-2034-4269, value 26.0). An hourly date_histogram with min_doc_count=0 over the window shows six consecutive empty buckets (2026-11-20T20:00Z, 21:00Z, 22:00Z, 23:00Z and 2026-11-21T00:00Z, 01:00Z), i.e. six missing hourly samples and roughly a 7-hour collection gap. So data is observed to stop at 19:10Z and resume at 02:10Z; the exact moment collection failed and the reason are not in the evidence. The last request ID before the gap is REQ-37-8A4F2, which is also the only in-window request_id that does not follow the REQ-NNNN-NNNN pattern used by the other 17 documents. No cause is attributable: cluster events in the window start only at 2026-11-21T04:23:43Z (nothing spanning the gap), there is no namespace for app-189, and the Prometheus target returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on both attempts, so collector/agent restart signals could not be checked. Whether the six samples were never written or were written and later removed cannot be distinguished with the available evidence.

claims.text: The index app-189-metrics-timeseries exists with health green, status open and docs.count 42 at the time of the query; it is the only index matched by pattern *, so no second/fallback metrics index was observed.
The index mapping declares @timestamp (date), host (keyword), metric_name (keyword), request_id (keyword) and value (float).

Inside the authorized window 2026-11-20T05:11:40Z–2026-11-21T05:11:40Z the index returned exactly 18 documents (total relation eq 18), all with metric_name cpu_usage, timestamped once per hour at :10 from 2026-11-20T06:10:00Z through 2026-11-20T19:10:00Z and then from 2026-11-21T02:10:00Z through 2026-11-21T05:10:00Z.

An hourly date_histogram (fixed_interval 1h, min_doc_count 0) over the authorized window shows doc_count 1 in the 06:00–19:00 buckets of 2026-11-20 and in the 02:00–05:00 buckets of 2026-11-21, and doc_count 0 in the buckets 2026-11-20T20:00Z, 21:00Z, 22:00Z, 23:00Z and 2026-11-21T00:00Z, 01:00Z.
The last document before the gap is @timestamp 2026-11-20T19:10:00Z, host server-3, metric_name cpu_usage, value 38.0, request_id REQ-37-8A4F2.
The first document after the gap is @timestamp 2026-11-21T02:10:00Z, host server-5, metric_name cpu_usage, value 29.0 -> 26.0 as written in the document (value 26.0), request_id REQ-2034-4269.
All 18 in-window request_ids follow the form REQ-NNNN-NNNN (e.g. REQ-0020-5441, REQ-1234-2682, REQ-2316-8693) except the last one before the gap, REQ-37-8A4F2, which has a different form.

A host rotation is visible across consecutive samples in the window (server-5, server-1, server-2, server-3, server-4, server-5, ... through server-3 at 19:10Z, resuming with server-5 at 02:10Z and continuing server-1, server-2, server-3).

Cluster events inside the authorized window span only 2026-11-21T04:23:43Z to 2026-11-21T05:10:46Z, contain no event group referencing app-189 or a metrics collector, and therefore contain no event whose own timestamp falls in the 2026-11-20T19:10Z–2026-11-21T02:10Z gap.
The cluster has no app-189 namespace; existing namespaces are app-102 (Terminating), default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo.

Six consecutive hourly write cycles at :10 (2026-11-20T20:10Z through 2026-11-21T01:10Z) produced no indexed document, i.e. the metric-writing job stopped writing to app-189-metrics-timeseries for about 7 hours rather than the samples being sporadic.

That the resume document at 02:10Z on host server-5 is exactly the host the observed rotation would have assigned next (server-3 at 19:10Z followed by server-4, server-5, server-1, server-2, server-3, server-4, server-5) suggests the hourly schedule kept running while six writes failed to reach the index; this is an inference from pattern, not observed job execution.

Nothing in the available evidence identifies what stopped the collection: the only events in the window begin at 2026-11-21T04:23:43Z, after the gap ended, and no namespace or workload for app-189 is present in the cluster, so a collector outage, an ingestion rejection or a later deletion of six documents remain equally consistent with the data.

gaps: The cause of the gap is unknown: no evidence in this Run shows the writing agent, its configuration, or an error at 2026-11-20T19:10Z–2026-11-21T02:10Z.

Prometheus was unavailable: get_metric_names for kube_pod_* / kube_deployment_* and for kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total both returned status error with reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so collector/agent restart, scrape-target health and Kubernetes restart signals at the gap time could not be checked.

The index holds 42 documents but only 18 lie inside the authorized window; the 24 earlier documents are outside the authorized window and were not queried, so whether the hourly cadence was gap-free before 2026-11-20T05:11:40Z is unknown.

Whether the six missing hourly documents were never indexed or were indexed and later deleted (retention, reindex, manual deletion) cannot be determined from the index, which has no alias, rollover or ILM information in the evidence gathered.
The significance of the anomalous request_id REQ-37-8A4F2 (the only non-REQ-NNNN-NNNN value, and the last record before the gap) is unknown; it is not shown to be a cause or an effect.

No application logs for the metric writer were inspected because no pod or namespace serving app-189 exists in the cluster; change_history is not an integrated source in this Run, so no change record around 2026-11-20T19:00-20:00Z could be checked.
next_steps: Identify the collector/agent that writes app-189-metrics-timeseries (the only visible producer label is host server-1..server-5) and check its own logs for export failures around 2026-11-20T19:10Z–2026-11-21T02:10Z.
Check index-level retention/ILM and any reindex or delete operations against app-189-metrics-timeseries for the 2026-11-20T20:00Z–2026-11-21T01:00Z buckets.
Verify from the producer side whether the six :10 hourly samples (20:10Z–01:10Z) were emitted, to distinguish 'never written' from 'written then removed'.
Confirm the meaning and handling of request_id REQ-37-8A4F2 with the metric pipeline owner, since it breaks the REQ-NNNN-NNNN convention on the last record before the gap.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind.
